Tip: Use your before a noun for something that.

Use your before a noun for something that belongs to the listener.

  • your: Use your before a noun for something that belongs to the listener.
  • my: Use my before a noun for something that belongs to the speaker.
  • his: Use his before a noun for something that belongs to a boy or man.

Prepositions of Place

A1 · core

Use in, on, under, and next to to say where things are.

in | on | under | next to

"A platform is the place where you get on a train."

Use on for something touching the top of another thing.

Jump to transcript

"Go there now if you are in a hurry."

Use in for something inside another thing.
